Others for the shortlist are Stellar Symphony, Phildante, Technology and Derby Rock.

Prior to that effort, the locally-trained five-year-old had shown a decent level of ability and, if recapturing her best form, she can be expected to go close. Coming from the point-to-point fields, Mistyburn and Kershaw are both of interest. The former is out of six-time winner Queen Althea and joined Philip Rothwell after winning at Necarne in May, while the latter was a good second on his sole start to date at Loughanmore. Kool Runnings, Governors Rock and Bradley's Row are also respected.

The one that appeals most is DODGE CITY who has improved with each run and has been handed a workable looking mark for handicap debut. Yet to go beyond 6f Brian Meehan's colt should find 7f up his street and it was encouraging he handled cut so well when runner-up last time. Boiling Over is next on the list. He was slightly disappointing last time when raised to a class 2 novice having gone off favourite but can be given another chance to get back on an upward trajectory having gone so close prior in a decent maiden at Sandown. Commander's Intent looks next best. A winner on second start over 7f with cut he stepped up on that effort last time and merits his place at the top of the weights. There should be more to come and he should play another big role

selections.comment: Most of those with experience have failed to show anything worth getting excited by and some of the newcomers have a good chance of figuring first time out but it could be worth trusting SUNSET ON LEROS can raise the bar a little higher having gone well on debut behind some useful looking sorts. The second that day, Wild Desert, went on to be a close-up third in a Group 3 next time. Marco Botti's colt looks the most solid option. Of the newcomers Allegresse and Double Eagel make most appeal and both could easily challenge for honours. George Boughey's Double Eagle is just preferred but second choice goes to Calchas. Ralph Beckett's colt was disappointing on debut having atttracted fair market support but deserves a second chance to deliver and he can improve past Ciao Capo, next best of those with experience.

selections.comment: JACK DANIEL is not the most reliable but appeals as the most likely winner. A winner on soft ground and ideally suited to a mile, conditions are set for Steph Hollinshead's gelding to show best having found his level again after steadily slipping down the handicap. He went well last time staying on over 7.5f at Chester and three runs back went very close on the AW off a pound higher than today. He's entiled to go close. Lockdown Lass poses a serious danger. A course and distance winner in soft ground she's taken time to find her form this term but a fourth last time out at Chester (3/4l behind the selection, 2lb worse off) was much better and she could be returning to the sort of levels shown back in 2023 (only run six times since). Miss Willows is interesting but is verty hit or miss and Autumn Festival is on a dangerous mark if rediscovering his best but Flag Of Love is feared more. Tim Easterby's filly has struggled since handicapping off stiff marks butb has slipped 17lbs in five runs having run over inadequate trips the last thrice. His two best career efforts came in deep ground and now back up to a mile and with plenty of juice in the ground a much better effort is on the cards

selections.comment: A chance is taken with ASTRONOMICA who should relish conditions having won both starts on soft ground and performing to peak levels on both good to soft and heavy ground. She'll need to build on her comeback run last time off a six month layoff but she made a much bigger leap from first to second start last term. She rarely puts in a poor effort and can be trusted to bring her A-game today and can justify support. Harbour Vision has decent cliams and is feared most, especially now returned to a mile. However, he's best on the AW and, although he handles cut, deep ground poses a question and the selection looks more solid under the forecast conditions. Ey Up Its Jazz is at the peak of his powers and could find a little more, if so he's entitled to go close under suitable conditions and just gets preference over Electric Lightning who could go well at more rewarding odds

That was a first try at this trip but is probably best forgotten and suggested this trip would be well within his compass when rallying late over 1m2f on second start in March. He was out of his depth next time in a Listed event but back in calmer waters should be tough to beat. Stem is a huge danger on season comeback having opened his accoun t on first time of asking last term in deep ground. That was over 7f but the manner of the win (9 1/2l) strongly suggests he'll be suited to trips of 1m2f plus. He should put up a stiff challenge. Codiak, one of two newcomers, is well-bred and and could figure in the shake-up on debut

selections.comment: Plenty in with a shout but top-weight NOVELLO LAD has the loudest. Paul Midgley's gelding landed a second career win last time over 6f having knocked on the door twice prior over 7f. The step back up to 7f holds no fears and although both his wins have come on a sound surface he showed on a few occasions that he handles soft ground. Kept to this grade he can add to his tally. Nigel Tinkler's gelding appeared to have a bit left up his sleeve last time and the only question mark surrounds the going. His only run on soft was poor, on second start when beaten 18l in a novice but that was over 7f which stretches his stamina and he hadn't got the hang of things and he won with a fair bit of cut at Carlisle on penultimate start. He should go close despite the slight step up in grade. Dark Rosa is a serious danger. In fair form all five runs this term on decent ground he could raise his game back on softer conditions having gained his only win with cut last September and with good efforts either side of that on heavy and soft. Better runs from Haazeez and Ran Amok look possible but Stirrup Cup is taken to hit the frame. He's struggled in three runs this year but wasn't beaten too far last time and has decent prospects at the weights based on a nursery win on soft last September and these conditoins might just spark a revival

And Silver Wraith is very unexposed; therefore, he could run well and finish in the places here.

selections.comment: PUBLISH was very well talked about after his debut 2nd at this venue a few weeks back; many felt he should have won the contest had he gotten a bit more luck in running. He was denied a clear run on multiple occasions and did have to switch left inside the final furlong, so he did do well to run on and claim 2nd spot, only getting beaten by half a length in the end. If all goes his way, he will be hard to peg back in this contest. Colin Keane is currently serving a suspension; therefore, James Doyle takes the reins here; therefore, this looks like a pretty straightforward ride for him. Catullus was another one who was unlucky in running on debut last time, but he did make nice headway and was only beaten by just over 3 lengths by two well-bred animals. He can come on for that run and go well here for the boys in blue. And Bosom Pals has the experience on the rest of these with two career runs to his name; however, he will have to settle with filling the places behind two well-bred rivals.

selections.comment: ORION'S BELT looks to be well regarded by the yard, and although an odds-on favourite when beaten on debut at Salisbury back in June, she did look as if she needed the run that day and ultimately was only beaten by a length in what looked to be a decent enough contest. She put that experience to good use next time out when winning by 4 lengths at Newmarket, making all and soon keeping on well in the closing stages to win going away in the end. Her trainer really likes her, and the fact he has pitched her into a listed company already would suggest they think there is a lot more to come from her. Jennifer Jane hails from a yard that is going well at present, and she was a very nice winner of a fillies maiden stakes at Kempton last time. She takes a step up in class here, but she looks a talented sort who will run well here. And Hope Queen won as she liked on debut at Beverley; when well odds-on in the market, she is sure to run well here for a yard that does very well with their youngsters.

selections.comment: PENDRAGON has an excellent record on turf with 3 wins in 4 career starts on the grass; he has been in brilliant form of late as he bids for the four-timer here. In typical Sir Mark Prescott fashion, he has improved markedly after a gelding operation and a step up in trip; a winner off the mark of 69 back in June, he is now rated 94 and looks like he could go in again here. A very impressive 4 1/4-length winner at this venue a few weeks back, he does have the 9 lb raise in the weights to deal with here, but given the nature of his win last time, it would suggest he can go in again. Tarriance is the unexposed type who could be anything; he has only had the three career runs to date and really looks the sort who could progress the further up in the trip he goes. He can run well in this but might have to settle for a 2nd place effort once again. And Tremorgio has been running well in this sort of company of late; he can go well once again and claim 3rd spot for the 2nd time this season.

selections.comment: A tight contest where most of the field can be given some sort of chance. It is veteran dual purpose performer DOUGLAS DC who appeals most though at potentially generous odds returning from the flat where he has been in good form. It was the same story when last seen over hurdles in the autumn and though his strike rate is a worry he has dropped to a very attractive mark. Strong staying course specialist Scintillante is feared most with his penultimate run franked in a hot weekend handicap while veteran chaser Grey Skies isn't ruled out at big odds. He is thrown in on his old chase form and hinted at a revival last time when allowed an easy lead.

She was a point winner before placing behind a classy rival who was completing a hat trick in a bumper. Plenty more is expected for a top trainer/jockey combination over hurdles and she may get off the mark at the first time of asking.

selections.comment: JER BATT was in behind Existent in the Epsom Dash last time, but gets a 2lb pull with that rival and looked full of running when caught too far back at Chester prior so he gets the nod here in ideal conditions. Existent does have a long losing run to get over but has been knocking on the door consistently for some time, he has just 1 win from 39 turf starts but ought to be thereabouts once more eased back in grade. Making up the places is Tan Rapido who was too far back and never got a run at Newbury in his penultimate start but went on to win last time at Chelmsford when back in trip. Solar Acclaim can challenge, he was back to form last time in soft conditions.

King's Scholar was suited by the step-up in trip over 1m5f at Hamilton and impeded last time out when probably wanted a better test, the Ed Walker yard is in form and he could go close. Miller Spirit can make up the places, he was briefly impeded at Ascot last time and relishes soft ground.

She will need to prove both her stamina for 7f and suitability for soft ground though and both of those factors may play into the hands of SKYDANCE. She remains a maiden but her debut form was franked in the Anglesey and she put up a big effort at Group level last time behind the favourite for next year's Guineas. Composing represents a top stable with a fine record in this and though the form of her maiden win is nothing special she isn't ruled out.

She showed a good attitude last time and the softer ground holds no fears so she is strongly respected but could be vulnerable to the top weight ALICE MONET on her handicap debut. She might not have beaten much last time in a claimer but she couldn't have been more impressive and looks to have been let in lightly by the handicapper. There is plenty of competition for the lead which should guarantee her a strong pace over the shorter trip. Refreshment met trouble last time in his hat trick bid but could also get back on track with the easier ground no issue.

Red King finished behind Happy Pharoah here earlier in the summer but could reverse that form on the softer ground and complete the tricast.

selections.comment: Former Graded hurdle winner MAKE GOOD snapped a long losing run last time and is fancied to defy an 8lb higher mark. He's never won off a mark as high as this 68 on the flat but at his peak over hurdles was rated as high as 137 so should have mileage in his rating and the easier ground will be in his favour. Ranting And Raven has been steadily progressing and despite being a maiden she looks on a good mark. If her stamina holds up over this longer trip she can threaten in the first time cheekpieces. Consistent pair Makaiah and Curious Bride complete the list of dangers though the soft ground is a worry for the latter.

selections.comment: Front Door Famous was only beaten by a useful more experienced pair on debut with the winner in particular looking a classy type. If making usual improvement he is entitled to be on the premises in a weaker contest but it is CROOKED TANNIE who is marginally preferred. He has an absence to overcome but he has a big experience edge on his rivals and sets the standard on form on his latest placed effort in a handicap. He also boasts some good course form and can account for Complete Fiction who was poor on his last hurdles outing but needed the run. His flat exploits suggest he has more to offer in this sphere though that may eventually come in handicaps.

selections.comment: The huge drift told a story on MUMMY DERRY's debut over hurdles but the fact she was thought well enough of to contest a Graded contest on debut speaks volumes. She was unsuited by the soft ground that day having previously landed a bumper on good and is taken to bounce back on her return from a break. Local trainer Paul Nolan usually leaves here with a winner and Tequila Talkin' is feared most with the form of her placed effort franked by a classy winner. She finished ahead of Hillhead Runner that day and can confirm that form with improvement expected for that initial experience.

She shaped with promise on all of her novice runs notably in a hot contest in the UK last time where she met trouble and finished with running left. Knockraha Eagle did much the best of those forcing a strong pace last time and if ridden slightly more conservatively here she can provide the biggest challenge along with To The Wire. That rival travelled powerfully here last time in a good race before his stamina gave way late over half a mile further.
